debug.storageNote: The escape room runs inside the iframe. LLM Explorer stores crystals and progress outside the game.
debug.finalDescription: The final door brings together the language-model journey. Learners place five crystals, form the final crystal, then solve the final lock.
debug.finalStep1: Place crystals around the language model

feedback.tokenDefault: A Token can be a whole word, part of a word, punctuation, or another text piece.
feedback.tokenInspected: Good. The tokenizer must split text into Token pieces before the lock can use it.
feedback.tokenised: This verified example came from the Qwen2.5 tokenizer. Now transfer the idea to a different word.
feedback.tokenSelection: Selection ready. Activate the lock to compare it with the tokenizer.
feedback.tokenChoose: Choose one Token split before activating the lock.
feedback.tokenIncorrect: Not quite. There is no single split that every tokenizer must use. Different tokenizers can split the same text in different ways.
feedback.numbersDefault: Choose the job performed by the ID.
feedback.contextDefault: The door scanner is offline. Inspect the console to find out what it needs.
feedback.contextInspected: Console inspected. Activate the context scanner to reveal the tokens the lock can read.
feedback.contextScanned: Scanner active. The glowing frame is the current context window.
feedback.contextSelection: Selection ready. Check the glowing window boundary, then unlock the door.
feedback.contextNeedScanner: Inspect the console and activate the context scanner before opening the door.
feedback.contextChoose: Choose the group of tokens inside the glowing context window.
feedback.contextIncorrect: Not quite. Look at the edges of the glowing context window. Only the tokens inside that frame are available in this example.
feedback.connectionDefault: The connection console is offline. Inspect it to find out what the door needs.
feedback.connectionInspected: The lock combines information from several token positions. But the connections are not all equally strong.
feedback.connectionScanned: Scanner active. Follow each arrow toward the focus token, then compare their thicknesses.
feedback.connectionSelection: Selection ready. Compare the shown arrow thicknesses, then unlock the door.
feedback.connectionNeedScanner: Inspect the console and activate the connection scanner before opening the door.
feedback.connectionChoose: Choose the token with the thickest arrow pointing toward opened.
feedback.connectionIncorrect: Not quite. You do not need to guess which word seems most important. Compare the arrow thicknesses in the connection pattern.
feedback.predictionDefault: The prediction console is offline. Inspect it to find out what signal the door needs.
feedback.predictionInspected: The machine compares several possible next tokens before the door can respond.
feedback.predictionRan: Prediction signal ready. Higher probability means more likely right now, not guaranteed.
feedback.predictionSelection: Selection ready. Read both the largest probability and the machine note, then unlock the door.
feedback.predictionNeedMachine: Inspect the console and run the prediction machine before opening the door.
feedback.predictionChoose: Choose the statement that best matches the displayed prediction signal.
feedback.predictionCorrect: Correct! “book” has the highest probability shown, so it is currently the most likely option. But a higher probability does not guarantee that it will be chosen.
feedback.predictionIncorrect: Not quite. Look at both parts of the clue: 46% makes “book” the most likely option shown, but probability is not a guarantee.
feedback.patternDefault: The training console is offline. Inspect its records to see how the model learned.
feedback.patternInspected: Good. The console contains records from earlier training examples.
feedback.patternRevealed: The examples affected what became more likely later. Now explain why.
feedback.patternSelection: Selection ready. Use the records and later prediction to activate the lock.
feedback.patternNeedPrediction: Inspect the training console and reveal the later prediction before opening the lock.
feedback.patternChoose: Choose the explanation that connects repeated examples, learned patterns and later predictions.
feedback.patternCorrect: Pattern restored. Repeated training examples can contribute to learned patterns that influence later predictions.
feedback.patternIncorrect: The engine stays locked. One example does not become a stored answer. Think about what repeated training examples can change over time.

exit.fusionComplete: Final crystal formed. The Final Lock is now active.
exit.complete: Final lock solved. Training happened earlier; during use, tokens, context and connections lead to one next-token prediction.
exit.ready: The order is correct. Solve the Final Lock.
exit.orderPrompt: Put the five ideas in order to solve the Final Lock.
exit.placePrompt: Place all five crystals around the model door.
exit.needsCrystals: The final room needs every room crystal.
exit.reset: Final lock reset. Place the five crystals, then rebuild the path.
exit.cardsCleared: Cards cleared. Rebuild the learning-to-prediction path.
exit.fusionStarted: Five crystals placed. Fusion sequence started.
exit.placedProgress: {{count}} / {{total}} crystals placed. Keep powering the Language Model Door.
exit.slotOccupied: That slot already has a card. Drag the card to swap, or choose an empty slot.
exit.slotsFull: All five slots are filled. Check the order, then solve the Final Lock.
exit.cardPlaced: Card added to a slot. Keep filling the empty slots.
exit.unreadableCard: I could not read that card. Try dragging it again, or click it instead.
exit.wrongDropArea: Drop that card inside the Final Lock slots.
exit.cardRemoved: Card removed. Try the order again.
exit.dropOnSlot: Drop the card onto a slot or inside the matching console.
exit.waitFusion: Wait for the final crystal to form.
exit.placeAllFirst: Place every crystal around the Language Model Door first.
exit.fillSlots: Fill every empty slot before solving the Final Lock.
exit.incorrectOrder: The final lock is still closed. Check the order and try again.

completion.title: Congratulations — the Language Model Door is open!
completion.intro: You restored all five crystals and rebuilt the path from learning to prediction.
completion.summary: Language models process text as Tokens, use available Context, combine information through Connections, make a next-token Prediction, and rely on Patterns learned earlier during training.
completion.guide: Guide note: you solved the final lock by connecting the ideas — not by treating the model like a person.

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.body: Text is split into smaller pieces the model can process.

context.title: Context
context.body: Earlier available Tokens help shape what may come next.

connections.title: Connections
connections.body: Information from different Token positions can be combined.

prediction.title: Prediction
prediction.body: The model compares possibilities and selects a next Token.

patterns.title: Learned patterns
patterns.body: Training happened earlier and shaped the model's later predictions.
